summary: A light on a bare rock beside Enterprise Channel near Victoria, lit in 1906 after the Clallam disaster and rebuilt in 1970 as a slim concrete 'apple core' tower.

access.note: Part of the Trial Islands Ecological Reserve, closed to the public; landing needs a permit, no docking facilities.

notes_for_editor: Rests on Lighthouse Friends (secondary, copyrighted; paraphrased) plus Department of Marine reports and the heritage statement. 'Staines Point' name and lens maker/Birmingham origin are from Lighthouse Friends only; the 1906 report names a Paris maker in the same section but the column is ambiguous, so not stated. The 1902 and 1904 stranded vessels' names are not given in the snippets read. J. McDonald (1907-08) matched by column position in OCR tables. The 1922 report notes a tug submerged near Trial Island; omitted. Not checked: Daily Colonist 1895, Graham's Keepers of the Light, Parks Canada page (returns only a banner). Wreck of the Clallam not examined beyond the heritage statement. Keepers list in Lighthouse Friends gives 'Iain Cloquhoun' (typo); story uses Colquhoun as in its own text. Fiscal years: 1906 report = FY to 30 June 1906; 1907-08 catalog volume = nine months to 31 Mar 1907; 1908-09 volume = FY to 31 Mar 1908; 1909-10 volume = FY to 31 Mar 1909. Okell's 22 Aug 1906 and McDonald's salary read from page images (pp.176, 191). LF's 'ten years' after 1895 is really eleven.
